subject: Urban Planning
title: Microgrids: Decentralized Power
description: A 60-second lesson on Microgrids: Decentralized Power.

hook.text: When Hurricane Sandy hit New York, most of Manhattan went dark. But NYU's campus stayed lit — powered by its own microgrid.

buildup.text: Microgrids generate and distribute power locally. When the main grid fails, they disconnect and run independently.

discovery.text: Military bases, hospitals, and universities already use microgrids. They combine solar, batteries, and small generators.

twist.text: Utility companies oppose microgrids because they reduce dependence on the central grid — and the utility's revenue.

climax.text: Community microgrids could power entire neighborhoods with rooftop solar and shared batteries, reducing grid dependence.

punchline.text: The big grid went down. The small grid kept the lights on.

quiz.question: What makes microgrids resilient during major storms?
options: They use stronger cables that resist wind and water damage
They disconnect from the main grid and operate independently
They store emergency power in underground bunkers
